summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, diastolic heart failure, and a history of venous thromboses and anticoagulation was admitted after developing sinus tachycardia with hypotension during dialysis. She was managed in the ICU initially with IV and oral metoprolol, followed by addition of diltiazem to control her heart rate. A CT scan ruled out pulmonary embolism, and her rhythm stabilized without progression to atrial fibrillation. Warfarin was held due to an elevated INR of 3.8 and later restarted at 2 mg daily. Dialysis was continued with reduced fluid removal to prevent recurrence. She had a mild upper respiratory infection managed supportively. Given her complex medical needs, she was discharged to extended care with adjusted medications, including lower-dose metoprolol and diltiazem, and plans for INR monitoring and follow-up on a small lung nodule.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
